newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB offers grain trucking premium to Pacific port.
newsitem.headline: CWB offers grain trucking premium to Pacific port.

text.p: Three trucks hauled grain to the port in Prince Rupert, B.C., from the Peace River Valley this week since the Canadian Wheat Board offered a C$5 a tonne bonus to alleviate a rail shipment backlog to Pacific ports.
"Three trucks are already en route and there's another eight to 10 that are possible to move in the near future," CWB spokeswoman Tracey Thompson said.
Forty-four ships waited to load grains and oilseeds at Canada's Pacific ports Wednesday. One ship had waited 48 days.
The weather- and locomotive-shortage-induced backlog has forced the CWB to pass on February and March sales.

"Until the end of March the CWB's offering a C$5 per tonne trucking premium to farmers in the Peace River district to haul their grain by truck to Prince Rupert and the incentive will come from the pool account revenue," Thompson said.
The CWB already faces more than C$15 million in demurrage fines for the ship backlog on the Pacific coast since early January.

"In addition, farmers trucking their grain to Prince Rupert can receive an additional C$2.20 per tonne which comes from the rebate CN (Canadian National Railway Co ) provides to the CWB to move grain to that port," she said.
